summary: Healthnauts is a daily crew health monitoring app for long space missions. In January 2026, NASA ended a mission early because of a crew member's health. On the way to Mars, evacuation is not possible and messages to Earth take up to 22 minutes each way, so crews must notice problems early and act on their own. Healthnauts organizes health data around NASA's five RIDGE hazards, compares every value with NASA-STD-3001 limits, and shows clear alert levels with short "what to do now" steps that open the full details in one tap. A 1-minute morning check-in, a reaction time test and a gamified health tree turn self-monitoring into a daily habit. The app runs fully in the browser, without depending on a connection to Earth. All demo data is simulated.
details:
Healthnauts is a daily crew health monitoring app for long space missions. On the way to Mars, evacuation is not possible and messages to Earth take up to 22 minutes each way, so crews must notice problems early and act on their own. The app organizes health data around NASA's five RIDGE hazards (radiation, isolation, distance, gravity and closed environments):

- Overview: one sentence about today, a "Next up" routine, a 3D body to open each area and up to 10 panels the astronaut chooses.

- Alerts: five levels (Normal, Advisory, Caution, Warning, Emergency) plus Unavailable, always with icon and text, based on NASA-STD-3001 limits. Each alert shows "what to do now" steps and opens the details in one tap.

- Emergency: vehicle safety conditions (cabin pressure, oxygen) open a full screen alert with an acknowledgement countdown. Without acknowledgement, it escalates to the Crew Medical Officer and a report is queued to Earth with the real communication delay.

- Daily routine: a 1-minute morning check-in in steps (sleep, sleepiness, fatigue, mood and stress), a reaction time test (PVT-B), exercise and weigh-in.

- Journey: a health tree that grows with completed tasks.

How it works

A rules layer in JavaScript evaluates every reading against its source and returns the level and message; the interface never decides a level by itself. The same rules run in the browser and in an optional Node/Express server that represents the onboard computer, so the app works without a connection to Earth.

Benefits and intended impact

Crews can spot health problems early and know the next step without waiting for Earth. Daily, low-effort self-monitoring builds a habit across long missions. The same approach could support people far from medical care on Earth.

How it is creative

- Gamification without punishment: XP rewards doing the task, never the health result, and the tree never dies, so a bad day is never a failure.

- Each astronaut is compared with their own usual range, not only with a population average.

- Alerts are built for action: one tap from the alert to the next step.

Factors the team considered

- Use official NASA limits first, and label every external reference or team proposal.

- Communication delay and loss of contact with Earth.

- Alert fatigue: clear levels, icon plus text, never color alone, and Emergency reserved for vehicle safety.

- Privacy of mood and stress data, and not diagnosing any condition.

- Readability for a tired astronaut: high contrast, short text, mobile layout.

Tools

React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Framer Motion, Zustand, three.js, Node.js/Express, GitHub Pages, 104 automated tests. AI assistance: Anthropic Claude (details in the README).

Limitations

Prototype with simulated sensor data. Not tested with astronauts. It does not diagnose any condition. Mood, stress and sleep quality use prototype 1 to 10 scales.

Live app: https://mendezinxd.github.io/NasaSpaceAppsChallenge2026/
